name: digitalplay.work creative-arts taxonomy
about: A small ontology for free, playful creative tools. Every tool belongs to one section and one subcategory, carries facet values, and links to techniques, a movement or era, and the things that inspired it. Influences are stated as short factual lines and never imitate a named living person.

sections.name: Music
sections.summary: Instruments built from art manifestos, music theory, natural patterns and studio methods. Bring your own sounds.

sections.name: Art
sections.summary: Shapes, marks, colour and pattern. Push things about until a picture turns up.
suggestedNext: Dot Field: turn your photo into halftone dots or pointillist dabs
Exquisite Corpse: a three-part drawing game where each player only sees a sliver
Stencil Cutter: cut layered stencils and print them in two colours

sections.name: Design
sections.summary: Grids, colour and type for posters, pages and things people actually read.
suggestedNext: Letter Builder: draw a whole alphabet from a kit of modular parts
Repeat Tile: design a seamless wallpaper tile from your own doodles
Pictogram Kit: make a set of simple icons for a place you know

sections.name: Coding
sections.summary: Code as a material for drawing, systems and toys. Small rules, big surprises.
suggestedNext: Bounce Box: tweak gravity, friction and bounce on your own drawn shapes
Pixel Sprite Lab: design and animate an 8×8 character
L-System Greenhouse: grow plants from rewrite rules

sections.name: Writing
sections.summary: Words as loose parts: cut them up, constrain them, turn them into games.
suggestedNext: Constraint Dice: roll a rule (no letter e, seven words, only questions) and write to it
Story Cubes Maker: make your own picture dice from words you choose
Haiku Counter: syllable-aware drafting for short forms

sections.name: Moving Image
sections.summary: Animation, montage and stop motion from things you draw or film.
suggestedNext: Flipbook Studio: frame-by-frame drawing with onion skins, export a GIF
Stop-Motion Booth: grab frames from your webcam and play them back
Zoetrope: build a spinning optical toy strip and print it

sections.name: Games and Play
sections.summary: Make games, change rules and play with play itself.
suggestedNext: Board Game Forge: design a roll-and-move board and print it
Rule Swap: take a classic game and change one rule at a time
Tiny Platformer: draw a level and play it straight away

sections.name: Performance
sections.summary: Prompts and scores for theatre, movement and live art.
suggestedNext: Event Score Cards: write and shuffle one-line instructions for a performance
Movement Dice: roll actions, levels and speeds for a short dance
Shadow Theatre: cut-out puppets against a lit screen

sections.name: Photography and Image
sections.summary: Camera play and darkroom-style effects on your own pictures.
suggestedNext: Photogram Maker: lay objects on virtual blueprint paper
Contact Sheet: shoot a roll of twelve and choose one
Pinhole Simulator: see how aperture and distance change a picture

sections.name: Making
sections.summary: Print, cut, fold and build: paper, textiles and tinkering.
suggestedNext: Paper Net Builder: design a 3D shape and print its net to fold
Weave Planner: plan a woven pattern on a virtual loom
Pop-Up Card Lab: simple pop-up mechanisms to cut and fold

sections.name: Nature and Science
sections.summary: Patterns in leaves, weather, tides and numbers.
suggestedNext: Sky Diary: log the sky's colour each day and build a year-long strip
Leaf Symmetry Lab: photograph leaves and compare their halves
Sun Clock: make a sundial for your exact location

sections.name: Ideas
sections.summary: Tools for thinking sideways: prompts, constraints and reflection.
suggestedNext: Prompt Deck: write your own deck of creative prompts and draw one a day
Idea Collider: smash two random things together and see what you get
Done List: a calm log of what you made this week

values.label: First go
values.description: Open it and play. No experience needed.

values.label: Getting going
values.description: A few ideas to pick up; rewards a second visit.

values.label: Deep dive
values.description: Lots of controls; give it an evening.

values.label: AI optional
values.description: Works without AI. If you want, paste your own Gemini key; it stays in your browser.

relationships.description: Every tool lives in exactly one section.
Plain-English techniques a player practises, e.g. symmetry, loops, cut-up.
The movement, tradition or era the idea comes from, stated factually.
Short factual lines naming a work, idea or tradition. Never a living person's likeness, voice or style imitation.

rules: No living artist's name or likeness in a tool name, branding or AI prompt that imitates a named person.
Influences appear only as short factual inspired-by lines.
No copyrighted quotes, lyrics, scores, images or fonts without a licence.
No personal data collected. Tools run in the browser and work offline.
Visitor API keys are pasted by the visitor and stored only in their own browser.
